extracted.intended_audience: applied empirical economists and policy researchers studying education and development
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and reporting choices used in an applied empirical impact-evaluation paper (tables, figures, robustness checks, and econometric specifications) studying school construction and schooling outcomes. Covers dependent variable definitions, fixed effects, clustering, placebo and robustness checks, IV strategies, and presentation conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent variable measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent variables are measured as new schools of a given type created per village–year or per district–year, and sometimes normalized per 1,000 children in 1971 or expressed as a share of all schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'new schools of a given type created per village–year', 'formal madrasa at all instruction levels built per district–year as a fraction of all formal schools', and normalization 'per 1,000 children in 1971'. Notes explain that differences in observations across columns reflect years with no entry of the given school type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary estimating equation and imputation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate average of post-SD-INPRES-entry coefficients τ using the robust imputation method from Borusyak et al. (2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table notes: 'This table reports estimates of the average of post-SD-INPRES-entry coefficients τ in equation (2) computed using the robust imputation method from Borusyak et al. (2024).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed effects inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appropriate fixed effects such as village FE, district FE, year FE, grade-level FE, year-of-entry FE, district × survey-year FE, district × grade-level FE, and cohort FE as required by the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables repeatedly indicate which fixed effects are included (ticks). Notes: 'All specifications include district fixed effects, grade-level fixed effects, year-of-entry fixed effects' and similar formulations across specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control variables and interacted controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Include predetermined controls (e.g., number of public/Islamic schools in baseline years, 1971 children population, 1971 enrollment rate, exposure to other programs) and interact these controls with year fixed effects when indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'post-1972 dummy interacted with the 1971 children population, the 1971 enrollment rate, exposure to the water and sanitation program, and the baseline number of elementary, junior secondary, senior secondary madrasa.' Also interactions like '1959 Islamic Schools × Year FE' and 'Initial Schools × Year FE'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clustering and robust standard errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Report robust standard errors clustered at an appropriate level (village or district) and state the clustering choice for each panel/specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: 'Robust standard errors are clustered by village in panels (a)–(c) and by district in panel (d).' Many tables conclude with 'Robust standard errors clustered by district.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use significance stars and report their thresholds: * p<0.1, ** p<0.05, *** p<0.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every table includes the star notation and the p-value cutoffs in the notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report sample sizes and basic summary stats
rubrics_metrics.description: Always report number of observations (e.g., number of village–years, district–years, individuals), dependent variable mean, and R-squared where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables include rows 'Number of Village–Years', 'Number of District–Years', 'Number of Individuals', 'Dep. Var. Mean', and 'R2'. Notes explain variation in sample sizes across columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness checks: removing controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess robustness by re-estimating baseline specifications after removing time-varying controls included in baseline estimation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel (b) description: 'removing the time-varying controls included in the baseline estimation, i.e., public and Islamic schools in the village by 1959 (panel b)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness checks: sample window variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-estimate using alternative panel windows (e.g., shorter panel 1968–1983) to check sensitivity to sample period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel (c) uses a shorter panel window 1968–1983 and additionally controls for interactions of year FE with public and Islamic schools in the village as of 1967.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness checks: clustering level
rubrics_metrics.description: Check sensitivity of inference by clustering standard errors at alternative aggregation levels (e.g., district vs village).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel (d) description: 'clustering standard errors by district.' Compare with panels clustered by village.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placebo tests in other periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform placebo tests by restricting analysis to pre- or post-periods (e.g., 1960–68 and 1990–98) to show effects are unique to the target period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix Table A.7 re-estimates specifications for periods (a) 1960–68 and (b) 1990–98. Notes: 'The SD Entry variable turns on the first year ... entering in the given period and then stays on thereafter.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Heterogeneity and interaction specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate heterogeneity by interacting treatment intensity with predetermined district-level characteristics (e.g., high potential rice yield, high waqf endowment, Islamic vote share in 1950s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables include interactions like 'SD × high potential rice yield', 'SD × high waqf endowment', and specifications interacting INPRES × Islamic vote share (1950s) × post-1972.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placebo and alternative outcome checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the heterogeneous supply response is unique to the period of interest and does not arise for other outcomes or periods (e.g., public primary school entry in other periods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix text: 'Placebo Check on Table 3 ... does not arise for entry of public primary schools in other periods (1960–68 and 1990–98) when rice prices were lower.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumental variables strategy and instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: When addressing endogeneity, instrument potentially endogenous entry with valid supply-side instruments (e.g., waqf endowment base, potential rice yields, Muslim population share) and report IV estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix Table A.22 instruments 'Islamic elementary school construction (× exposed cohort and INPRES) instrumented by the waqf endowment base, potential rice yields, and the Muslim population share (× exposed cohort and INPRES).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak-IV diagnostics and first-stage reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report first-stage strength diagnostics (KP first-stage Wald statistic) and weak-IV LM test p-values alongside IV results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table A.22 reports 'KP 1st stage Wald statistic' and 'KP 1st stage LM test, p-value' for IV specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of interaction terms for substitutability/complementarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret sign of interaction terms to infer substitutability or complementarity (e.g., negative interaction between public and Islamic elementary entry implies substitutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix text: 'A negative interaction term implies that the two types of schools are substitutes.' Empirical results and magnitudes are discussed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and construction of survey/regression outcome variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully define outcomes to reflect data limitations (e.g., Susenas records final year of schooling and only allows madrasa not pesantren; transitions defined as graduated from one level and transitioned to but did not graduate from next level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: 'Susenas ... only captures the type of the final year of schooling completed by respondents' and 'These are the only transitions that we can observe in Susenas...' Table notes consistently describe outcome construction and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple data sources and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and document multiple data sources (e.g., IFLS, Susenas, administrative data from MEC and MORA, SIAP registry, MORA registry, Bazzi & Blattman commodity price database) and state coverage/limitations of each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table A.16 summarizes Islamic education rates across IFLS, Susenas, and administrative sources and explains representativeness differences (e.g., IFLS covers 83% of population).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure construction and inference presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Present figures showing trends, SDID or synthetic DID estimates, counterfactual lines, weights used for pre-period averaging, and plot confidence intervals with clustered standard errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes for figures: 'The dashed diagonal line indicates the counterfactual parallel trend, and the arrow indicates the estimated effect.' Figures report 90% confidence intervals with standard errors clustered at the district level and show weights used to average pre-INPRES periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain economic context and external shocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Document and present relevant external shocks or context (e.g., world rice price shock) that may coincide with policy timing and could affect interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A.2: 'Rice Price Shock. Appendix Figure A.6 demonstrates the large shock to the world price of rice coincidental with the SD INPRES policy.' References to Bazzi (2017) and Bazzi & Blattman (2014) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain and justify sample differences across specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly explain why the number of observations differs across columns and panels (e.g., years with no entry of the given school type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: 'Differences in the number of observations across columns reflect years with no entry of schools of the given school type.'
